Video Resurfaces Of #BloodHoundQ50 Not Caring Droppin His Loc While On Stream With The Worker Looking Worried 😭 He Really Didn’t Care 💔🕊️ 

BloodHound Q50, born Mikquale T. Cooper, was a rising Chicago drill rapper who became one of the most talked-about young artists from the city’s newer generation. He began taking music seriously around 2023, gaining attention through songs like “Big 3,” “Coffin,” and “Splash Bros.” His career continued growing following his collaborations with close friend BloodHound Lil Jeff, and he eventually signed with Signal Records, an imprint associated with Columbia Records. 

Q50 was especially close with BloodHound Lil Jeff, and after Jeff’s d**** in 2024, Q50 said the loss pushed him to take his rap career even more seriously. He went on to release his debut project Long Live My Brudda He Prolly Kilt Yo Brudda in 2025 and followed it with Get Back or Die Trying in August 2026. His music accumulated millions of streams as his name continued growing beyond Chicago. 

Sadly, Q50 d*** on September 13, 2026, at just 22 years old following a shooting in Chicago’s Fuller Park neighborhood. Chicago police said the case remained under investigation, with no arrests announced in the initial reports. 

Today, September 25, 2026, BloodHound Q50 was reportedly laid to rest, as his family, friends and loved ones gathered to celebrate his life and say their final goodbyes. Public posts from today document his funeral, though I haven’t found a major news outlet reporting details of the service yet. 

Long Live BloodHound Q50 🕊️💔
